notes: EARNINGS, on the v2 plate kit. The print against what was expected, what
moved, and what it means — in the vertical set only.
There is no stamp. A verdict card is a CALL, and the register is
anti-Cramer by construction: he describes and the viewer decides. What
was a stamp is the closing plate's own line now.

A STATIC PLATE MAY HOLD. The ceiling was written when every plate in the kit boiled; 44 of the 140 are `playback: static` now, because a figure that moves is a figure being re-read. What keeps a data beat short is the ceiling itself, and it is set to what a seventy-second cut of ten beats actually gives each one.

ALTERNATE ORDERS CAME BACK WITH THE BEAT MARKERS (items 2 and 26). `sign-off-first` put the closing card ahead of the hook and stays retired: the first second is the ticker and the move. The orders below may move anchored beats, because a marked script says where each beat starts and the cut follows its markers; an unmarked script is only offered the orders that keep the beat sequence it was written to.

WIPES MARK A CHANGE OF SUBJECT (item 13): a shot with `enter: wipe` is wiped in, sweep and page alternating, at most three a short; every other cut stays hard. A wipe on every cut would be a signpost on every cut, which is none.

shots.notes: The hook card, second treatment — earnings is not the daily short and should not open on the same picture. THE TICKER AND THE MOVE IN FRAME ONE (item 6): `move` takes the day's signed move and counts up over the first half second while the hook is spoken; `sub` takes the rest of the summary. A summary that does not lead with a signed move leaves `move` empty and keeps the whole summary in `sub`.

alts.notes: The fifth treatment: the hook on a full field with the ticker at the foot, so the eye lands on the sentence before the chip. The same slots. `hook-card-t4` is not here on purpose — it leads with the figure at 240pt, and the next beat is that figure.

shots.notes: The number that printed, at the size it deserves.

alts.notes: The same figure with a detail rule under it, for a print that has a verdict to carry.

shots.notes: Print against consensus, stacked. The delta slot holds eight characters and takes the gap.

alts.notes: Print and consensus side by side rather than stacked. Same slot names, so the binds carry; `detail-1` and `detail-2` go unfilled.

What was expected over what came out, as two stacked panels. `body-1` is bound REQUIRED on purpose: the plate's caution is that without a real prior expectation it reads as a comparison against a number it invented, so the rotation only reaches for it when the script carries the consensus. The gap on the divider stays empty — it is a figure nobody wrote, and the pipeline does not compute one.

shots.notes: Every row up at once — an earnings cut has no time for a walk down them.
What they said about next year, in the card drawn for a term and its meaning.

alts.notes: Guidance as a line worth pulling out rather than a term and its meaning.

shots.notes: The line the print actually means, told to camera in close-up.

meme.notes: The one place for a meme: the tail of the verdict, once both sides of it are on screen and before the close.

alts.notes: The two-sided beat as said-against-happened. Names its slots nothing like `both-true`, so it restates the binds; `wrong` and the three labels are the kit's own and take no binding.

THE OTHER WAY TO END. All three vertical formats closed on `structure/closing` every time, so every short in the channel signed off on the same drawing. The conclusion is a line worth pulling out by definition, and `quote-pull`'s body is the only other 9:16 plate wide enough to hold one without narrowing what the writer may write — `structure/end-card` holds 58 characters against closing's 136, so rotating onto it would have shrunk every conclusion in the channel to suit the alternate.

ONE THING AT STATEMENT SIZE. The original close has three lines and a script has one conclusion, so two of them were always empty. The handle moves up to the kicker: this plate's date label sits inside the caption band, where the last spoken words would run over it. Its detail line stays empty — the plate's own caution is not to pad it.

orders.name: guidance-first
orders.notes: The guide is the news on some prints and the quarter is the footnote: guidance straight after the hook, then the print against the estimate. Cut only for a script whose markers put `guidance` second.

orders.name: turn-early
orders.notes: The pivot before the years: Dennis says what the beat does not tell you, then the sheet proves it. Cut only for a script marked in this order.
